stock_name: Kamchatka flounder - Bering Sea / Aleutian Islands
catch_age_evidence: 2024 BSAI SAFE reports fishery catch biomass and fishery length compositions; it does not report a fishery catch-age series. Sparse survey ages do not supply catch numbers-at-age.
survey_age_evidence: BSAI SAFE reports survey biomass and length data; age compositions are sparse (EBS slope in 2002 and 2012; Aleutian Islands in 2010, 2016, 2018, and 2022), not a continuous age-specific index.
weights_evidence: The 2024 assessment describes growth and length-weight biology; age-specific weights require extraction from the official model inputs or outputs.
maturity_evidence: The 2024 report cites the maturity schedule of Stark (2011); an age-specific vector requires source extraction.
mortality_evidence: The 2024 assessment fixes natural mortality at 0.11 per year.
timing_evidence: The assessment uses annual BSAI trawl-survey observations; a fractional within-year timing is not established by the reviewed source.
output_evidence: The 2024 SAFE provides age-structured assessment results, but this does not supply missing observed catch-at-age inputs.
decision_reason: Ineligible for the age-input screen: no fishery catch-age series or source age composition was verified; sparse survey ages cannot support catch numbers-at-age. The 2024 report is the latest full production assessment; later material is projection-only.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART 10002; 2024 Model 16.0b is the latest full run located. Sparse survey age samples and age-structured model outputs are not substitutes for fishery catch-age data.

stock_name: Arrowtooth flounder - Bering Sea / Aleutian Islands
catch_age_evidence: The 2022 production assessment uses catch biomass and fishery length compositions; its source review found no accepted fishery age-composition likelihood. Existing canonical data are partial.
survey_age_evidence: The 2022 report describes survey age samples in selected years, but they do not replace missing fishery catch-age observations.
weights_evidence: See the existing BSAI arrowtooth source review for fixed biological inputs and the unresolved age-specific observation arrays.
maturity_evidence: The 2022 production report documents female maturity and fixed sex-specific M; see the canonical stock review.
mortality_evidence: The 2022 source review reports fixed M of 0.2 for females and 0.35 for males.
timing_evidence: Annual assessment and survey timing details are recorded in the existing source review; no new age-specific catch observation is supported.
output_evidence: The existing canonical record contains partial reported inputs and outputs; the 2022 report provides age-structured assessment results.
decision_reason: Matched to the existing BSAI arrowtooth stock and not a new case. Ineligible for an age-data translation because the fishery likelihood uses catch biomass and length compositions, with no verified fishery age-composition input.
notes: NOAA:10003 maps to afsc_arrowtooth_flounder_bsai; Stock SMART lists Reinhardtius stomias, while the official report and canonical record use Atheresthes stomias. The existing canonical assessment record is partial; do not count this inventory row as new.

catch_age_evidence: The 2025 data review and 2026 draft list total fishery catch biomass and fishery length compositions, not fishery age compositions or catch-at-age. Length compositions alone do not establish catch-age inputs.
survey_age_evidence: The 2026 draft reports GOA bottom-trawl age compositions for 1993-2025 with survey biomass; these can inform an age-specific survey index but do not establish catch-at-age.
weights_evidence: The 2025 data review and 2026 draft document age-length transitions and updated weight-at-age biology; the exact production-run matrices need source extraction.
maturity_evidence: The 2025 data review and 2026 draft describe maturity assumptions and the recommended fixed-M model; final run-specific biological matrices remain to be checked.
mortality_evidence: The recommended 2026 Model 25.0 fixes M at 0.20 for females and 0.35 for males; Model 25.1 estimates sex-specific M as a sensitivity.
timing_evidence: The GOA bottom-trawl survey is a summer survey; the report does not give a single observation fraction for the annual model, so translation timing would be an explicit approximation.
output_evidence: The detailed 2026 assessment draft reports age-structured outputs; the final October 2026 SSC report selects Model 25.0 for management advice. The full SAFE chapter remains pre-dissemination draft material at review date.
decision_reason: Ineligible under the source-age screen: the detailed current report lists catch biomass and fishery length compositions but no fishery catch-age observations. Survey age compositions do not fill that catch-data gap; the detailed 2026 report is still a draft.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART snapshot says 2024 and lists Reinhardtius stomias, while the assessment report uses Atheresthes stomias. The latest full assessment reviewed is 2026; the October SSC selected Model 25.0 for management advice, though the detailed SAFE chapter was still a draft on 2026-10-29.

catch_age_evidence: The 2017 report documents three fishery catch series (mink-food, fillet, discard) in tonnes and limited sex-specific age compositions from the fillet fishery. The age samples are sparse (1986-1991, 1998, 2003-2005, 2013); they are not annual catch-at-age. The report describes reconstructed landings/discards and lists the native .dat file, but that file was not found among public downloads.
survey_age_evidence: Four aggregate biomass survey indices are used. The NWFSC shelf-slope survey has sex-specific age-at-length data in 2003-2006 and 2013-2016, ages 1-28; the likelihood uses conditional age-at-length rather than a direct age-specific abundance index. The report lists model inputs, but the exact composition matrices were not publicly located.
weights_evidence: The report documents an externally estimated length-weight relationship and estimated sex-specific growth. It does not provide direct numeric weight-at-age input vectors; those would require the fitted growth and length-weight parameters from the unavailable native files.
maturity_evidence: Female maturity is a fixed length-based logistic ogive (slope 0.5, inflection 37.3 cm) carried forward from Rickey (1993). A numeric maturity-at-age series is not reported.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed by sex at 0.216 per year for females and 0.300 per year for males, the medians of documented lognormal priors.
timing_evidence: The assessment report says survey calendar-date effects were not investigated. A within-year survey fraction is unresolved.
output_evidence: The report provides annual spawning biomass and age-0 recruitment with standard deviations for 1916-2017, plus total biomass, age-3+ biomass, depletion and annual F rate. It names an annual sex-specific N-at-age CSV, but this output file was not located in public downloads.
decision_reason: Identity is distinct from the Bering Sea/Aleutian Islands, Gulf of Alaska and British Columbia units. Eligibility remains unresolved: the assessment has age data, but annual numeric catch-at-age is not available and its age likelihood is composition/age-at-length based. The 2017 report lists native model inputs and an N-at-age output CSV, but those files could not be recovered from the public Council listing or direct file URLs. Exact inputs and age-specific outputs need verification before selection.
notes: Stock SMART ID 10005 lists the scientific name Reinhardtius stomias; the official assessment identifies the stock as Atheresthes stomias. The 2017 Stock Synthesis update is the latest detailed fitted assessment located. Subsequent advice uses catch-only projections based on that model: the 2021 projection informs 2027-2028 specifications in the 2026 Council analysis. The projection updates catches, not the age-structured fit. See source_reviews/noaa_west_coast_arrowtooth.md.

catch_age_evidence: Native 2023 input has annual North and South catch totals and expanded commercial age frequencies. Catch-at-age can be reconstructed from fleet catch and age proportions; it is not supplied as the original likelihood observation.
survey_age_evidence: Triennial and WCGBTS have aggregate biomass indices. WCGBTS length and age samples support an approximate index age split; the Triennial survey has no age samples and cannot receive an age-specific index.
weights_evidence: Sex-specific weight-length relationships are estimated externally; growth is estimated in the model. Age-specific weights require documented conversion through growth.
maturity_evidence: The 2023 run uses a newly estimated female maturity-at-length ogive; an age-specific surface requires documented conversion through growth.
mortality_evidence: Sex-specific M is estimated with lognormal meta-analytical priors, median 5.4/Amax and log-scale SD 0.31; maximum ages are 32 years for females and 29 for males. Report.sso includes fitted M.
timing_evidence: Survey indices are recorded in July (month 7); native fleet settings encode survey timing 1007. Preserve the model convention and document conversion to fractional-year timing.
output_evidence: Fitted Report.sso includes annual N-at-age, F-at-age, catch-at-age and natural mortality. Its 2023 spawning output of 7.68553 trillion eggs matches the assessment report rounded to 7.686.
decision_reason: Eligible for source curation and translation with documented reconstruction of catch-at-age and WCGBTS index age splits, and age-scale derivation of weights and maturity. The Triennial survey has no age observations; this is not direct equivalence to the official likelihood.
notes: 2023 full benchmark is the latest completed detailed assessment located. The 2025 PFMC source is a catch-only projection; the June 2026 PFMC planning document still identifies 2023 as the completed benchmark. The official report, native inputs and outputs, and projection are cached under source_cache/discovery_noaa_petrale_10011; planning PDF SHA-256 661F039CAA92E078B4143E3B4FEF8AB38AEDE35F0E598F15A3372FE82733BCDA. Current US Pacific Coast unit is distinct from Canadian DFO petrale sole.

catch_age_evidence: 2024 empirical assessment reports aggregate catch only; no accepted catch-at-age series is reported.
survey_age_evidence: The current empirical assessment uses seasonal swept-area biomass, not an age-specific abundance index.
weights_evidence: No age-specific weight input for an age-structured production model was identified.
maturity_evidence: No age-specific maturity schedule is used by the current empirical assessment.
mortality_evidence: The accepted empirical assessment does not estimate age-specific natural mortality.
timing_evidence: Survey biomass combines seasonal spring/fall observations; no age-specific survey process to time.
output_evidence: 2024 report provides exploitable biomass and exploitation ratios, not comparable N-at-age or instantaneous F outputs.
decision_reason: Matched the current official witch-flounder unit. The 2024 assessment used seasonal swept-area biomass and aggregate catch, while the rejected analytical models do not establish a current age-structured input set; source review: nefsc_witch_flounder_unit.md.
notes: Source screening is based on the current/represented assessment distinctions in source_reviews/nefsc_witch_flounder_unit.md.

stock_name: Flathead sole - Bering Sea / Aleutian Islands
catch_age_evidence: 2024 operational update reports catch totals for 1963-2024 and marginal fishery age compositions for 2000-2001, 2004-2007, and 2009-2021. Composition is flathead sole only while several catch fleets combine flathead sole and Bering flounder.
survey_age_evidence: The 2024 update reports aggregate biomass and conditional age-at-length survey data for 1982, 1985, 1992-1995, 1999-2019, and 2021-2023. An age-specific index would require a documented reconstruction from CAAL, length composition, and biomass.
weights_evidence: The 2024 model uses estimated sex-specific growth and an externally estimated weight-length relationship; age-specific weights are available from the pinned model run.
maturity_evidence: The 2024 update reports an externally estimated age-based logistic maturity ogive (50% at age 9.7; 95% at age 12.8).
mortality_evidence: The 2024 update fixes M at 0.2 per year for both sexes.
timing_evidence: Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands trawl surveys are summer surveys in a one-season annual assessment; an exact tinyAM fractional timing is not specified in the brief update.
output_evidence: The 2024 report and pinned revision bafa7658d31e0b99fe11d626a58e1c01807c69ee provide fitted N-at-age and other Stock Synthesis outputs.
decision_reason: Eligible with documented reconstruction: the operational 2024 assessment supplies catch totals and fishery age compositions, plus survey biomass and CAAL/length information. Preserve the flathead-versus-combined-catch distinction and label any derived age-specific survey index as approximate.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART 10015 is the Flathead Sole-Bering Flounder stock-complex assessment. Treat as one assessment, not separate flathead and Bering flounder candidates; see discovery/source_reviews/noaa_flathead_bsai.md.

catch_age_evidence: The latest full 2022 assessment reports catch biomass and fishery length compositions but no fishery catch-age observations; later documents are projection updates.
survey_age_evidence: The 2022 model uses survey biomass and CAAL; its marginal survey age compositions are ghosted and excluded from the likelihood. No fishery age composition is reported.
weights_evidence: The 2022 assessment describes growth and weight-at-age biology; it does not supply the missing fishery age observations.
maturity_evidence: The 2022 report documents maturity and fixed M; see the detailed assessment and model materials.
mortality_evidence: The 2022 assessment uses fixed M=0.2; confirm details against its full source review before any translation.
timing_evidence: The GOA bottom-trawl survey is conducted in summer; any fractional timing would need to be stated as an approximation.
output_evidence: The 2022 full assessment reports fitted age-structured outputs; later 2024 and 2026 documents are projection updates.
decision_reason: Ineligible for the age-input screen: the latest full assessment reports catch biomass and fishery length compositions, while survey marginal age compositions are excluded from its likelihood; no fishery catch-age input was verified.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART 10016; use the 2022 operational run. The 2024 and 2026 documents are projection updates rather than new full age-data assessments.

stock_name: American plaice - Gulf of Maine / Georges Bank
catch_age_evidence: 2022 Run29F4 has catch totals and age proportions, but its status as the advice-run model is unresolved; 2026 MT3 age inputs are not recovered.
survey_age_evidence: Run29F4 has aggregate survey biomass and age compositions; the composition basis is available only for a research-track candidate.
weights_evidence: Run29F4 has survey-specific weights; current 2026 management-track biological arrays are not fully recovered.
maturity_evidence: Run29F4 maturity inputs are documented; updated 2026 management-track biology is not resolved.
mortality_evidence: Run29F4 mortality settings are recorded; selected 2026 advice-run status remains unresolved.
timing_evidence: Run29F4 and current MT3 timing details are not reconciled to a selected production run.
output_evidence: 2026 MT3 reports aggregate outputs, but its advice-run identity and age inputs remain unresolved.
decision_reason: Matched 5YZ American plaice. The 2026 MT3 source gives summary outputs but not age-specific inputs, while the detailed 2022 WHAM object is a research-track candidate whose advice-run selection is unresolved; source review: nefsc_american_plaice_5yz.md.
notes: Source screening is based on the current/represented assessment distinctions in source_reviews/nefsc_american_plaice_5yz.md.

catch_age_evidence: The 2023 model includes fishery catch biomass in tonnes for 1978-2023 and fishery length compositions for 1991-2023. It contains no fishery age composition; the assessment states that no otoliths were collected from catches. Catch-at-age cannot be reconstructed from source fishery inputs without transferring an age-length relationship from survey samples or using model-estimated growth.
survey_age_evidence: The GOA survey provides aggregate biomass in tonnes (triennial 1984-1999, biennial 2001-2023), survey length compositions, and conditional age-at-length samples for 1993, 1996, 1999, and 2003-2021. Combining same-year survey length and conditional age-at-length observations can support a marginal survey age composition; the conditional samples are not themselves an independent age-specific abundance index.
weights_evidence: The model derives weight-at-age from estimated growth and a weight-length relationship. No observed fixed weight-at-age vector is listed among the assessment inputs.
maturity_evidence: The model uses an age-based logistic maturity relationship; it is not a fixed maturity-at-age input vector.
mortality_evidence: The 2023 Model 19.3.1 estimates sex-specific natural mortality in historical and 2014-2023 time blocks. The 2023 report gives point estimates and uncertainty summaries.
timing_evidence: The native data file records survey month 6 (June); the assessment uses spawning month 5. These are distinct timings. A tinyAM survey fraction would need to be documented as a translation approximation.
output_evidence: The 2023 SAFE tables report age-3+ biomass, female spawning biomass, age-3 and age-0 recruitment, and M estimates. The report says a separate numbers-at-age time series is available, but that file was not recovered; the pinned repository contains the assessment inputs and 2025 projection files, not a 2023 Report.sso or age-specific output table.
decision_reason: NOAA Stock SMART ID 10021 is a new Gulf of Alaska unit, distinct from the existing US West Coast Dover sole unit. The official 2023 Model 19.3.1 is age- and sex-structured, but it fits fishery length compositions and has no fishery ages. A catch-at-age series would require transferring survey age-at-length samples to fishery observations or using fitted growth; neither conversion is verified as a source-supported catch input. Mark ineligible for the current age-input screen; retain its verified source information for possible future use.
notes: The latest full assessment is the 2023 Model 19.3.1 update using data through September 2023. The 2025 harvest projection used this fitted assessment with updated catches. The 2023 report identifies Stock Synthesis 3.30.21, while the pinned CIE accepted-run files identify 3.30.13 in their headers; record this version discrepancy. See discovery/source_reviews/noaa_goa_dover_sole.md.

catch_age_evidence: The 2021 Stock Synthesis data file contains retained catches for two fisheries and year/sex/fleet age-composition observations, ages 1-60. Age compositions are available rather than complete observed catch-at-age; catch-at-age can be reconstructed from totals, compositions and weights. The assessment reports limited new fishery age readings after 2010.
survey_age_evidence: Four aggregate survey-index series are included. The native data file includes conditional age-at-length records for the NWFSC Slope and WCGBTS surveys and derived marginal WCGBTS ghost compositions. The latter are not independent likelihood observations. An age-specific index would require a documented conversion from the aggregate index and age data.
weights_evidence: The two-sex model uses size-based growth and weight-length relationships, not a fixed observed weight-at-age input. Derived age-specific weights are available in the official fitted model output.
maturity_evidence: The official model uses a length-based female maturity relationship and length/weight-based fecundity; derived age-specific biology is reported.
mortality_evidence: Female natural mortality is fixed at 0.108 per year; male M is estimated as an offset from female M. The fitted model reports the resulting values.
timing_evidence: The native input specifies survey timing months: AFSC Slope 10, Triennial 7, NWFSC Slope 9 and WCGBTS 8. These settings are available for review.
output_evidence: The official Report.sso includes numbers-at-age, catch-at-age, F-at-age and biomass-at-age, as well as aggregate biomass and recruitment outputs. Age-specific fitted outputs are not observed catch-age inputs.
decision_reason: No matching canonical US West Coast Dover sole stock was found. The public 2021 full assessment bundle provides native age-composition and survey age information, aggregate catch/index inputs, biological model files, and official age-specific population and mortality outputs. Mark eligible for source import and a documented age-structured approximation; this does not imply a like-for-like SS translation.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART ID 10022; one coastwide US stock unit, distinct from Canadian Dover sole. The 2021 assessment uses data through 2020. The 2021 model-file ZIP includes native inputs and fitted outputs; recent management projections reviewed remain based on the 2021 full assessment. See discovery/source_reviews/noaa_pacific_coast_dover_sole.md.

catch_age_evidence: The NOAA Stock SMART 10025 row is the 2005 broad Pacific Coast assessment, not a current assessment unit. The current 2017 Northern and Southern entries use the DB-SRA report, which uses regional aggregate catch histories in metric tonnes rather than catch numbers-at-age.
survey_age_evidence: The older 2005 assessment used relative trawl-logbook indices and a California age-1 abundance index, but no age- or length-composition data. Those are not inputs to the current 2017 DB-SRA, and this broad legacy entry is superseded by separate current Northern and Southern rows.
weights_evidence: The current DB-SRA does not use age-specific weights. It uses life-history inputs and age at maturity; no current weight-at-age surface was found.
maturity_evidence: The 2017 DB-SRA uses age at maturity of 3 years, not a maturity-at-age vector.
mortality_evidence: The current DB-SRA uses a distribution for natural mortality as a life-history input; it does not estimate annual or age-specific M.
timing_evidence: The current catch-based DB-SRA has no survey observation series requiring survey timing.
output_evidence: The current DB-SRA reports MSY distributions and management harvest specifications, not annual N-at-age, F-at-age, or M-at-age. The 2027-28 official specifications still cite the 2017 DB-SRA.
decision_reason: NOAA Stock SMART ID 10025 is the older 2005 broad Pacific Coast entry. The current 2017 assessment register has distinct Northern (14804) and Southern (14805) units. Treat the old row as an ambiguous historical identity linked to both current entries, not as a third current stock. The current DB-SRA inputs are not age-disaggregated.
notes: The 2005 Stock Synthesis assessment modeled California and Oregon-Washington separately. The 2017 DB-SRA superseded those model projections for harvest specifications. Review current entries NOAA:14804 and NOAA:14805 together; see discovery/source_reviews/noaa_starry_flounder.md.

stock_name: Alaska plaice - Bering Sea / Aleutian Islands
catch_age_evidence: 2024 Model 24.1b uses total dead catch; fishery age compositions are available only in 2000, 2002 and 2003, not as a complete catch-at-age series.
survey_age_evidence: EBS survey biomass is available; bottom-trawl age compositions cover intermittent years and acoustic-trawl age compositions cover 1994-2024. These are conditional compositions, not an unconditional abundance-at-age series.
weights_evidence: Native Model 24.1b files contain annual fishery/stock weight-at-age calculations; the report cross-check and distinction from input compositions are documented in source_reviews/afsc_alaska_plaice_bsai.md.
maturity_evidence: The applied run uses a fixed female maturity-at-age vector across ages 0-25+; source vector is retained with the native assessment inputs.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed at 0.13 per year for both sexes; the report and native controls agree.
timing_evidence: EBS survey observations use month 7 (fraction 0.5); timing is specified in the production input files.
output_evidence: Official Model 24.1b Report.sso and SAFE report provide annual N-at-age, F-at-age, SSB, recruitment and biomass outputs, 1975-2024.
decision_reason: Matched the existing BSAI Alaska plaice record. The official 2024 model and outputs are verified, but full catch-at-age is not supplied and fishery age compositions occur in only three years; composition-only evidence does not meet the required catch-age or reconstructable-source threshold.
notes: Model: final SSC-selected 2024 Model 24.1b, Stock Synthesis 3.30.22; native repository revision 96b65a032cda06013376a8c8a11b553ebf194784. Source cache and remaining composition/weight/uncertainty details are documented in source_reviews/afsc_alaska_plaice_bsai.md. Excluded from new age-input candidate pool despite age-structured fitted outputs.

catch_age_evidence: The 2025 assessment updates commercial and recreational catch totals in metric tonnes through 2024. It is an area-swept 30+ cm biomass assessment, not a catch-at-age model; no catch numbers-at-age are used.
survey_age_evidence: The assessment uses fall area-swept biomass estimates from NEFSC, MDMF, and MENH surveys, with updated q = 0.79. These are 30+ cm aggregate biomass observations, not age-specific abundance indices or age samples.
weights_evidence: The area-swept biomass model does not use weight-at-age inputs.
maturity_evidence: The area-swept biomass model does not use maturity-at-age inputs.
mortality_evidence: The 2025 report describes 30+ cm exploitation rate, not age-specific natural mortality; M-at-age inputs are not part of this area-swept model.
timing_evidence: The biomass indices are from fall surveys. The report does not provide a model sampling fraction within the year.
output_evidence: The report provides 30+ cm biomass and exploitation-rate time series; 2024 biomass is 4,537 mt and exploitation rate is 0.044. It does not report N-at-age, F-at-age, or M-at-age.
decision_reason: NOAA Stock SMART ID 10028 is the current Gulf of Maine unit. Its latest 2025 management-track assessment updates the 2022 area-swept biomass method, rather than an age-structured assessment. It has no age-based inputs or age-specific outputs and is ineligible for the age-structured candidate set.
notes: Stock SMART assessment ID 14073 is an Operational assessment using the area-swept biomass method with data through 2024. The 2025 report was compiled in August 2025 and posted by ASMFC in January 2026; see discovery/source_reviews/noaa_winter_flounder_gom_sne.md.

catch_age_evidence: 2022 RunSpring22 native input contains catch-at-age for ages 1-6 and 7+; the 2025 WHAM update has summary outputs only.
survey_age_evidence: Native data include NEFSC/DFO spring indices and age-specific NEFSC fall index streams; timing is labelled 1 January.
weights_evidence: Native input contains annual catch weights and population weights by age.
maturity_evidence: Native VPA input contains annual maturity-at-age proportions.
mortality_evidence: M fixed at 0.3 per year across ages and years in RunSpring22.
timing_evidence: Native survey records are labelled 1-JAN and retained at fraction 0.0.
output_evidence: 2022 report provides SSB, age-1 recruitment and FFull for 2012-2021; N-at-age/F-at-age outputs were not recovered.
decision_reason: Matched Georges Bank winter flounder. The 2025 assessment is latest but summary-only; the separate official 2022 RunSpring22 record supplies native age inputs and aggregate SSB, recruitment and FFull outputs, already represented in the database; source review: nefsc_winter_flounder_georges_bank.md.
notes: Source screening is based on the current/represented assessment distinctions in source_reviews/nefsc_winter_flounder_georges_bank.md.

stock_name: Winter flounder - Southern New England / Mid-Atlantic
catch_age_evidence: The 2025 ASAP update uses commercial and recreational catch data through 2024. Its report tabulates fleet landings/discards and aggregate catch for assessment in metric tonnes for 2015-2024, but does not publish the age-specific catch arrays or age-composition sample counts.
survey_age_evidence: The 2025 report updates research-survey abundance indices and shows biomass-index series, but provides no age-composition arrays or age-specific abundance index values. Current-run source arrays were not recovered.
weights_evidence: The report states that projections use mean weights-at-age averaged over the most recent five years; the numerical current-run arrays were not included in the recovered report.
maturity_evidence: The report states that projections use maturity-at-age averaged over the most recent five years; the numerical current-run arrays were not included.
mortality_evidence: The report identifies natural mortality as an important uncertainty and states the 2011 benchmark increased M from 0.2 to 0.3. The 2025 update says data structure, settings, and assumptions were unchanged; the native 2025 M vector or input file was not recovered.
timing_evidence: The report identifies spring/fall NEFSC and state survey series, but does not provide the current model timing table or survey-year fractions.
output_evidence: The report gives aggregate SSB, fully selected F and recruitment through 2024; 2024 estimates are 2,787 mt, 0.048, and 6,211 thousand fish. Approximate 90% lognormal intervals are plotted. It does not provide annual N-at-age, F-at-age, or M-at-age outputs.
decision_reason: NOAA Stock SMART ID 10030 is the distinct SNE/MA winter flounder stock and the latest assessment is the 2025 ASAP management-track update with data through 2024. The report confirms an age-structured model and age-specific projection biology, but does not provide the current run’s catch-age and survey-age inputs, numeric biological arrays, or timing table. Keep age-input eligibility unresolved pending recovery of the native 2025 model data.
notes: Stock SMART assessment ID 14072 is an Operational ASAP assessment. The public report is marked a draft working paper for peer review only, but the 2025 results were presented to the ASMFC Management Board for 2026-2028 management decisions. The 2025 report states that data structure, model settings, and assumptions were unchanged. See discovery/source_reviews/noaa_winter_flounder_gom_sne.md.

catch_age_evidence: The final 2026 assessment reports fishery catch biomass in tonnes from 1982 through August 2026 (Table 7 says August 29; page 9 says August 22 for the terminal catch cutoff), and sex-specific fishery age compositions in 1992, 1995, 1999, 2003, 2005, 2007, 2009, 2010, 2012 and 2014-2024. survey_age_evidence: The RACE bottom-trawl survey provides separate eastern and western-central biomass indices for 1984-1999 (triennial) and 2001-2025 (biennial), with conditional age-at-length data in 1984, 1987, 1993, 1999 and biennially from 2001-2025. Marginal age compositions are not in the objective function; an age-specific survey index would be a documented reconstruction, not the native likelihood. Table 7 ends in 2025 while page 11 labels 112,824 t as a 2026 survey estimate; verify the year.
weights_evidence: Sex- and area-specific growth is estimated. Fixed weight-length relationships are female alpha 1.35e-6, beta 3.44963 and male alpha 2.18e-6, beta 3.30571; weight at age depends on the growth curves. Confirm the exact final-run weight scale before import.
maturity_evidence: Female maturity uses a logistic size-at-maturity relationship: 50% at 351.7 mm, with slope 0.0392 per mm, converted to age using survey-based mean length-at-age.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed at 0.17 per year for females and males; M is not estimated.
timing_evidence: The assessment is annual. The available proposed-run file has one 12-month season and assigns survey biomass observations to month 7, but it ends in 2024 and is not the final 2026 run. The SSC notes survey timing was misspecified in the SS3-to-SPoRC bridge; verify the final-run timing before translation and do not infer a year fraction yet.
output_evidence: Appendix F reports Model 25.1 numbers-at-age for 1982-2026 by two areas and sex, ages 0-20. It gives no uncertainty intervals and does not state the number scale in the heading. The report also gives spawning-biomass and recruitment results; a numeric F-at-age surface was not located. M is fixed at 0.17, not an estimated output.
decision_reason: The official 2026 full assessment is a two-area assessment for the current Gulf of Alaska unit. The Plan Team recommended Model 25.1 for harvest specifications and the SSC supported the recommendation. The assessment documents age compositions, conditional survey age-at-length, biological inputs, survey indices and comparable population outputs. The source quantities support curation, with transformations and run-matched input details to verify before import.
notes: NOAA IDs 10058, 15410 and 15411 are grouped as one unit: 10058 is the legacy Gulf-wide entry; 15410 and 15411 are eastern and western-central area entries. NOAA ID 10059 Pacific Coast rex sole is a separate unit. The public AFSC repository at revision 453e1166e1bf83b9062fe228b93f2225b1cbe1aa contains proposed runs ending in 2024, not run-matched final 2026 files. The final-report-linked Appendix E attachment is marked draft; confirm its correspondence to the final model before importing values. catch_age_evidence: The 2023 production assessment includes catch biomass and fishery length compositions, with discards modeled separately from landings beginning in 2002. Its native data file has no fishery age-composition rows. survey_age_evidence: Three aggregate survey-index fleets are included. WCGBTS fleet 5 has conditional age-at-length observations in 2007-2019 (620 aged fish, per the report), alongside survey length compositions. maturity_evidence: Maturity-at-length is based on Hosie and Horton (1977); the report says the logistic slope was assumed from Abookire (2006). Translate to age only with a documented growth-based conversion.
mortality_evidence: The control file specifies a one-parameter natural-mortality structure. Confirm the active parameter status, estimate and uncertainty in the selected base-run outputs.
timing_evidence: The model uses one annual 12-month season and three survey fleets. Verify the exact within-year timing encoded by the final native input before assigning a tinyAM survey fraction; do not infer it from the survey field season.
output_evidence: The native run archive includes Report.sso with numbers-at-age, catch-at-age, fishing-mortality-at-age, biomass-at-age and fitted age-composition output enabled. catch_age_evidence: SEDAR 100 uses fleet-level landings and discards with commercial vertical-line and longline, and recreational, conditional age-at-length data. These are not direct catch-numbers-at-age observations. The DW-04 and DW-07 source files provide fishery age and length data from 1999-2024; reconstructing catch at age would require an explicit composition and growth-based conversion. Years and fishery strata vary with sample-size cutoffs.
survey_age_evidence: The assessment fits aggregate annual abundance indices, including early SEAMAP summer-fall trawl (1987-2008), late SEAMAP summer-fall trawl (2009-2024), and G-FISHER video. SEAMAP trawl age and length samples were available for 2008-2024 (N=519), but the assessment fits survey length compositions rather than an age-composition likelihood. G-FISHER has length compositions but no empirical ages. An age-specific index would therefore be a documented reconstruction, not a native input.
weights_evidence: The assessment uses length-based biology and estimates growth internally from age-at-length data. Weight-at-age is not a native supplied likelihood input; deriving it would require the assessment length-weight relationship and estimated growth.
maturity_evidence: Maturity is modeled as a fixed function of length, not as a supplied maturity-at-age vector. Deriving maturity at age would require the assessment growth relationship and would be an explicit approximation.
mortality_evidence: The reviewed assessment fixes target natural mortality at 0.36 per year and scales it by age with a Lorenzen relationship through modeled age 15. The review-panel revised base model fixes M at 0.36 and estimates stock- recruitment steepness at about 0.422.
timing_evidence: The model covers 1945-2024, starts at age 0, and uses age-composition bins 0-10+ while modeling population ages through 15. It assumes continuous fishing through the year and July 1 settlement. Exact within-year timing fractions for the abundance surveys were not established in the reviewed sources.
output_evidence: The review-panel revised-base tables report annual biomass, SSB in metric tons, exploited abundance ages 1+, age-0 recruitment, and SSB ratio for 1945-2024. Annual F is reported as a harvest rate (biomass killed divided by age-1+ biomass), not instantaneous F-at-age. The published report does not provide numeric annual N-at-age or F-at-age arrays; the tabulated series are point estimates.
decision_reason: Eligible for source curation: the completed SEDAR 100 assessment report and supporting data papers provide removals, fishery conditional age-at- length observations, aggregate abundance indices, survey age samples, biological relationships, mortality assumptions, and comparable annual population outputs. Catch-at-age, age-specific survey indices, weight-at- age, and maturity-at-age are not direct inputs and would require explicit reconstruction, so this is not yet a translation-readiness decision. The SEDAR page says the assessment was completed in September 2026, but the NOAA peer-review listing has no actual dissemination date and formal management adoption was not confirmed in the reviewed sources.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART lists an older 2020 assessment year; the latest detailed source is SEDAR 100, with data through 2024. The assessment is one Gulf-wide unit (sexes combined), modeled from 1945 to 2024 in Stock Synthesis 3.30.21.00. The final report contains the assessment-process model and a review-panel revised base model. No numerical records were imported and no selected-batch decision has been made.

catch_age_evidence: The 2024 SEDAR 82 research-track BAM uses commercial and recreational landings and discards with age and length compositions. Fishery age bins were 1-5+ during 1982-2014 and 1-8+ from 2015; they are compositions, not observed catch numbers-at-age. The AW01/AW02 papers document the fishery age and length inputs.
survey_age_evidence: The assessment uses one combined fishery-independent index from the SERFS chevron-trap and related trap-video surveys. DW05 provides annual index and age/length compositions for 1990-2021, with no survey in 2020. The review found the fitted index and age-composition data adequate; the survey age compositions can support an age-specific reconstruction.
weights_evidence: Growth information is estimated outside the assessment model and used with age-specific reproductive parameters. The assessment reports egg production rather than conventional biomass-based SSB; source weight-at- age inputs were not established in this screen.
maturity_evidence: Maturity and fecundity are age-specific components of the egg-production measure. The report describes mature-female proportions, batch fecundity, and spawning events by age; these are not a conventional maturity-only SSB calculation.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is age-dependent and time-invariant, derived using a life-history meta-analysis and the selected maximum age of 16 years. The review documents sensitivity of biomass and F outputs to this choice.
timing_evidence: The research-track model covers 1982-2021. The chevron-trap survey is conducted mainly May-September, with limited sampling outside that window. The model timing fraction for the combined annual index was not established in this screen.
output_evidence: The 2024 research-track assessment and peer-review report provide annual F and egg-production trajectories, reference points, and stock-status diagnostics. Egg production is called SSB in the report but is not biomass in tonnes. Numeric annual N-at-age and F-at-age output tables were not verified in this screen.
decision_reason: The 2024 SEDAR 82 research-track assessment has detailed age-based inputs and outputs and is suitable for further source review. However, the peer-review panel described it as suitable to carry forward to an operational assessment; NOAA lists no actual dissemination date, and its species page still says no formal South Atlantic assessment has been conducted. Current production/adoption status is therefore unresolved. Do not import this research-track run as current official production values unless later agency documentation confirms its use.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART row 10063 lists 2016. The newer SEDAR 82 run is a 2024 Research Track assessment with data through 2021, not confirmed as an operational assessment. Its egg-production definition of SSB differs from biomass SSB. No canonical record or numerical data were changed.

catch_age_evidence: The 2022 Stock Synthesis advice model uses annual fleet catch in mass and catch-at-size/size compositions for 1952-2020. The data-preparatory meeting explicitly states that catch-at-age was not planned or calculated. No age compositions are fitted, so the public catch and size data do not support the required source-based catch-at-age reconstruction.
survey_age_evidence: The advice model uses five aggregate relative-abundance indices with lognormal errors. No age-specific index or survey age composition is reported for the fitted model.
weights_evidence: The model uses a combined-sex von Bertalanffy growth model and the length-weight relationship 7.48e-06 * fork length(cm)^3.253. These support size-to-weight conversion but do not supply age compositions.
maturity_evidence: The model is combined-sex; 50% maturity is at 42 cm fork length and full maturity at 55 cm. SSB is the summed biomass of mature fish.
mortality_evidence: The advice uncertainty grid uses Lorenzen-scaled M-at-age hypotheses anchored to the M-at-age-6 value for each growth scenario.
timing_evidence: The model has an annual time step, with fishing throughout the year. Individual relative-abundance indices are adjusted for within-year timing; exact fractions require the electronic model inputs.
output_evidence: Official outputs include SSB and F trajectories and uncertainty-grid status estimates through 2020. The latest summary reports 2020 relative biomass ratio of 1.60 (95% interval 0.90-2.87) and relative F of 0.41 (0.19-0.89). The assessment paper plots estimated numbers-at-age, but no run-matched numeric annual N-at-age/F-at-age tables were located.
decision_reason: NOAA Stock SMART 10158 represents the Western Atlantic skipjack unit assessed by ICCAT in 2022; no canonical tinyAM stock record was found. The model is age-structured internally but fits catch-at-size, size compositions, and aggregate CPUE. The official data-preparatory report states no catch-at-age was planned, and no age-specific survey input is reported. Length compositions alone do not meet the age-disaggregated source screen, so this unit is ineligible for the current candidate set.
notes: The 2022 Stock Synthesis model covers 1952-2020, has one area, combined sexes, ages 0-6+, five fleets/indices, and 2-cm size bins over 20-156 cm. The advice combines nine runs spanning growth and steepness uncertainty. The latest ICCAT executive summary located says the last assessment was in 2022 and reports 2020 status; later MSE operating-model updates are not a new assessment fit. Checked source PDFs are cached under source_cache/discovery_iccat_western_skipjack_2022/ with checksums.

catch_age_evidence: The 2024 quarterly Stock Synthesis assessment fits fleet catch and length compositions, not observed catch-at-age or age compositions. A modeled age grid is derived through assumed growth; the report says reliable aging is unavailable, so converting the length compositions to catch-at-age would impose an unsupported reconstruction.
survey_age_evidence: Five aggregate abundance/biomass indices were considered. The reference model uses an echosounder-buoy relative-abundance index and one tag-recapture biomass estimate (2020 Q2, CV 0.3); neither is age-specific.
weights_evidence: Weight-at-age is derived from modeled mean length-at-age and the length-weight relationship 5.53e-6 * L^3.336; no observed annual weights-at-age series is reported.
maturity_evidence: Maturity and batch fecundity are specified by length, with maturity from the central EPO area; no observed maturity-at-age input series is reported.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is specified by length using Hampton (2000), with linear interpolation between length-class midpoints and a constant value above 65 cm.
timing_evidence: The model is quarterly over 2006-2023. Index and composition data are quarterly or assigned to quarters; tinyAM annual survey timing cannot be copied directly from this model.
output_evidence: The report presents quarterly recruitment with 95% confidence intervals, spawning biomass/ratios and exploitation-rate trajectories. NOAA Stock SMART reports 2023 SSB of 17,809 metric tonnes. IATTC generated run outputs are linked online, but its page prohibits public redistribution of the files and derivative content without IATTC permission.
decision_reason: NOAA Stock SMART 10160 maps to the IATTC Eastern Pacific skipjack 2024 benchmark, with terminal data year 2023 and full acceptance in the inventory metadata. The 2024 quarterly Stock Synthesis benchmark has age states but fits catch, aggregate abundance/biomass indices and length compositions; no observed age-specific inputs were found. It is ineligible for the current age-disaggregated candidate screen.
notes: The assessment is quarterly, combines sexes, and models ages 0-20+ quarters on a 1-cm population-length grid from 2-110 cm. The report states reliable aging is unavailable and derives age from assumed growth. Purse-seine compositions use 1-cm size bins (20-100+ cm); longline uses 5-cm bins (40-100+ cm). Detailed native run files are linked by IATTC but were not cached because of the redistribution notice. The report PDF is cached in discovery_iattc_eastern_skipjack_2024/.

catch_age_evidence: The 2025 catch-only assessment updates catch through model year 2023 and retains the 2023 benchmark age-composition likelihoods for model years 2008-2021. Fishery age compositions are based on California commercial samples and can be combined with fleet catch and weights at age for a documented catch-at-age reconstruction. Age groups are 0-8+; no age compositions are available after 2021.
survey_age_evidence: The model fits a summer Acoustic-Trawl (AT) aggregate biomass index and AT survey age compositions for 2008-2021. The inherited 2023 Stock Synthesis data file records the index at model month 1.6.
weights_evidence: Empirical weight-at-age is used for fishery and AT survey data. Survey weight-at-age is derived from acoustic-trawl abundance-at-length, a length-weight relationship and age-length keys.
maturity_evidence: The model uses a fixed age-specific maturity vector estimated from summer AT samples of 494 female fish, multiplied by a fixed fecundity vector.

catch_age_evidence: The 2024 update fits the BAM statistical catch-age model through 2023. It updates commercial handline, headboat, and general recreational landings and discards. survey_age_evidence: The fitted assessment uses five aggregate abundance indices: commercial handline, headboat, headboat discards, SERFS chevron trap, and SERFS video. maturity_evidence: Female maturity is a fixed input logistic curve with a supplied age-specific vector. The SEDAR 73 model calculates spawning output as eggs using maturity, female proportion, batches at age, and size-based fecundity; this is not conventional SSB in biomass units.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed over time and decreases with age using a Lorenzen curve. It is scaled to match cumulative survival over ages 4 through the oldest observed age (51) under constant M = 0.11 per year.
timing_evidence: The assessment is annual. A fractional within-year timing for the fitted survey indices is not specified in the reviewed production report.
output_evidence: The 2024 report publishes annual numbers at age (1000 fish), biomass at age (1000 lb), and instantaneous F at age (per year) for 1950-2023; the model age range is 1-20+, with age 20 as the plus group. weights_evidence: The report describes a shared length-weight relationship; no complete numeric weight-at-age series was recovered.
maturity_evidence: Age-based maturity is a fixed model input shown graphically; the numeric vector was not recovered.
mortality_evidence: For preferred 2021 northern rock sole Model 21.2, female M was fixed at 0.2; male M was estimated at 0.232 centrally and 0.254 in the west.
timing_evidence: The report describes GOA groundfish survey years and spawning seasons, but does not provide exact timing proportions for tinyAM.

decision_reason: Not eligible for the current tinyAM age-structured translation screen: the documented official model uses annual total catch split by species and fishery length compositions, not catch-at-age. notes: Gulf-wide legacy stock smart identifier; grouped with the other NOAA Stock SMART source rows for the same GOA northern rock sole unit. stock_name: Pacific ocean perch - Gulf of Alaska
catch_age_evidence: The run-matched 2023 model has fishery catch biomass in tonnes for 1961-2023 and number proportions at ages 2-24 plus 25+ in 17 sampled years (1990, 1998-2002, 2004-2006, 2008, 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020, 2022). The pinned repository also supplies fishery weight-at-age for ages 2-29 in grams per fish. A source-based catch-number reconstruction is possible only for composition years; unsampled years remain missing.
survey_age_evidence: The assessment has aggregate bottom-trawl biomass in tonnes for 16 years from 1990-2023, with standard errors, and age proportions plus sampling counts for 14 years (1990, 1993, 1996, 1999, 2003-2021 biennially). Survey weight-at-age is supplied in grams per fish, supporting an age-specific abundance reconstruction for shared survey years. The final model .dat and SAFE list 1990 ages; an auxiliary repository CSV omits that row and must not replace the run-matched input.
weights_evidence: Pinned 2023 repository exports separate model, fishery and survey weight-at-age vectors for ages 2-29 in grams per fish. The official model uses one weight vector in its biomass equations; a tinyAM reconstruction can use the source-specific fishery and survey vectors and must document that distinction.
maturity_evidence: The official model estimates a logistic maturity-at-age curve from two female maturity datasets (Lunsford 1999 and Conrath and Knoth 2013); maturity is not a fixed supplied ogive.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is estimated as one constant parameter with a prior mean of 0.0614 and prior CV 0.1; the fitted value is about 0.074.
timing_evidence: The official annual survey prediction uses abundance at the survey year without a separate within-year sampling fraction. The input value spawn month 5 is spawning timing, not survey timing. Exact survey timing is not specified; any tinyAM fraction is an explicit approximation.
output_evidence: The pinned run repository contains point estimates of numbers-at-age (1961-2023, ages 2-29), recruitment, F, total biomass and spawning biomass. The SAFE report and model repository include MCMC uncertainty for selected aggregate quantities and parameters; age-specific N intervals are not in the exported N-at-age table.
decision_reason: Provisionally eligible for source curation and a later tinyAM translation: run-matched catch totals, age proportions and fishery weights support catch-number reconstruction in sampled years; survey biomass, age proportions and survey weights support age-specific index reconstruction; the assessment has biological inputs, estimated M and age-specific outputs. The translation must retain missing composition years, account for the 25+ observation group and disclose likelihood and timing approximations.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART ID 11056 is a separate GOA unit from BSAI POP (NOAA:11055) and British Columbia POP (DFO). Stock SMART lists 2024, but the latest completed detailed fit located is the 2023 operational update, Model 20.1, with data through 2023. The 2025 full assessment was cancelled; a new GOA assessment was scheduled for December 2026 and had not been released by the 2026-10-29 review date. See source_reviews/noaa_goa_pacific_ocean_perch.md.

catch_age_evidence: IPHC-2026-TSD-031 provides directed-fishery age-frequency specimen counts by regulatory area, year (1993-2025), and sex; the 2026-06 table revision is later than the assessment vintage and 2025 is preliminary. The assessment overview states port otoliths are sampled in proportion to landings within area/year. Combining source proportions with TSD-007 landings supports a documented catch-at-age reconstruction, with age-specific weight conversion and run-vintage checks required; model input arrays are available only by IPHC permission.
survey_age_evidence: Public IPHC FISS individual records cover 1998-2025 and include age, sex, maturity, length, station, and year; 365,576 of 2,273,521 records have a resolved age. Modelled FISS NPUE is available by regulatory area for 1993-2025, in numbers per standardized 100-hook skate with CV and 95% intervals. Splitting that index by observed age composition is possible for sampled area-years; unsampled areas are not extrapolated. Ageing groups and the post-assessment 2025 data vintage must be checked before treating reconstructed series as run-matched inputs.
weights_evidence: The 2025 assessment overview describes sex-, area-, age-, and year-specific FISS and fishery weight-at-age, with population values smoothed across years. The public FISS file provides fork length and age, and IPHC publishes a length-weight relationship. These support a documented reconstruction, but the exact four-model input matrices are not in the public assessment bundle.
maturity_evidence: The 2025 assessment updated the female maturity ogive using histology from 2022-2024; the data overview reports a curve truncated below age 7. The public FISS records include maturity observations. The report provides the ogive graphically, so exact run-matched values need recovery or documented digitization before import.
mortality_evidence: The 2025 ensemble includes four model structures: female natural mortality is estimated in three models and fixed at 0.15/year in the coastwide short model; male natural mortality is estimated in all four. Preserve model-specific M treatment rather than treating the ensemble as one fixed-M specification.
timing_evidence: The FISS is an annual summer survey conducted across late May-September; the assessment is annual. Sources establish a seasonal window but not one common within-year sampling fraction. Any single tinyAM timing would be an explicit approximation, ideally using area/year survey dates.
output_evidence: The official 2025 assessment reports annual female spawning biomass with approximate 95% credible intervals, plus recruitment, age-8+ biomass, and fishing-intensity estimates. IPHC-2026-TSD-029 provides annual spawning-biomass series for each of the four assessment models (1888-2026) in tonnes or millions of pounds. Public numeric historical N-at-age and F-at-age arrays were not found.
decision_reason: NOAA Stock SMART 11082 and the DFO Pacific halibut inventory entry refer to the same IPHC Convention Area resource spanning Canada and the United States; neither maps to a canonical tinyAM stock, so these two inventory rows are one provisional new unit. The current official assessment is IPHC-2026-SA-01, a four-model 2025 assessment. Public commercial age frequencies, area-specific landings, FISS age samples, an area-specific FISS abundance index, biology, and annual SSB outputs support source-based age-input reconstruction, so the unit is eligible for source curation with explicit approximations. This is not an exact replication of the Stock Synthesis likelihood: run input files require permission, the public commercial-age table was revised after the run, and numeric historical N-at-age and F-at-age outputs were not located.
notes: NOAA inventory year 2024 and the DFO 2024 survey row are source metadata, not the latest assessment year. Use the IPHC 2025 assessment through its 31 October 2025 data cutoff; do not substitute post-run updates without checking them against the pinned run. The latest assessment and public source files are cached under source_cache/discovery_iphc_pacific_halibut/ with retrieval dates, table/document identifiers, and SHA-256 hashes.

catch_age_evidence: The 2026 ISC assessment fits fleet catch by year and quarter, reported in metric tonnes or thousands of fish, plus size compositions. It does not fit observed catch-at-age; catch-at-age in model outputs is derived and cannot replace a source age composition.
survey_age_evidence: The base case fits one aggregate standardized CPUE index, Japanese longline Area 2 Quarter 2 (F10, 1996-2024); it is a fishery index, not a survey. No age-specific index or age-composition likelihood is reported.
weights_evidence: The model uses non-sex-specific seasonal weight-at-length relationships (kg from fork length in cm). It does not report a fitted weight-at-age input; conversion would require the model sex-specific growth distribution.
maturity_evidence: Female maturity is assumed to be 50% at age 5 and 100% at ages 6+, based on length at 50% maturity of 86 cm fork length.
mortality_evidence: Base-case natural mortality is fixed by age and sex: a Lorenzen size-based schedule for ages 0-2, common to both sexes until age 3, then 0.38 per year for males and 0.49 per year for females.
timing_evidence: The population model is quarterly; spawning and recruitment occur in Quarter 2 (April-June). The fitted F10 index also represents Quarter 2. There is no survey timing because the base-case index is fishery-derived.
output_evidence: The 2026 report provides annual numeric estimates for age-1+ biomass, female SSB and recruitment through 2024, with uncertainty. Model-derived catch-at-age and sex-specific F-at-age are shown in figures; no historical numeric N-at-age table or machine-readable age-specific trajectories were found.
decision_reason: NOAA Stock SMART 11682 and the DFO North Pacific albacore listing identify the same transboundary ISC stock (equator to 55 degrees N; 120 degrees E to 100 degrees W), new to the canonical database. The latest production assessment is the 2026 ISC benchmark, based on data through 2024. Although its internal model is age- and sex-structured and reports age-specific fitted outputs, its accepted observations are total catch, aggregate fishery CPUE and length compositions. No source age composition is available to construct age-specific tinyAM inputs without inventing observations; screen this shared unit outside the current age-disaggregated translation set.
notes: ISC/26/ANNEX/08 supersedes the 2023 assessment; NOAA Stock SMART metadata still lists 2023, so the inventory year is retained as source metadata and not treated as the current production run. Canada is an ISC member and contributes fishery data to this shared assessment; DFO and NOAA entries are one biological unit, not two stocks. The official report is cached under source_cache/discovery_north_pacific_albacore/ with its retrieval date, pinned revision and SHA-256. ISC stock-assessment data files require an access request; the public report is the reviewed evidence.

catch_age_evidence: The 2025 single-area, two-sex model covers the combined Rougheye and Blackspotted management complex. It uses catch biomass in metric tonnes for six fisheries and conditional age-at-length (CAAL) observations from fishery sampling. CAAL data enter the likelihood; marginal age compositions are supplied for fit evaluation. Catch-at-age is not a direct annual input and would require reconstruction from catches and sampled age information.
survey_age_evidence: The native model includes indices for Triennial, Alaska slope, Northwest slope, and WCGBTS surveys, with survey age/length observations described in the report. The data file retains survey observation timing and age compositions. An age-specific abundance index is not a direct model input and would require a documented reconstruction from aggregate indices and age compositions.
weights_evidence: The model derives weight-at-age from its fitted growth and weight-at-length parameters; the native Report.sso includes biomass-at-age output.
maturity_evidence: The model uses a length-based maturity relationship documented in the 2025 report; age-specific maturity can be derived from the model growth surface if required for a tinyAM approximation.
mortality_evidence: Female natural mortality is estimated. Male natural mortality is fixed at 0.036 per year following likelihood-profile analysis; alternative M values are used in the report uncertainty scenarios.
timing_evidence: The native data file records observation months for survey series and the model has January spawning. Preserve each observation month when converting to fractional-year survey timing.
output_evidence: The native Report.sso includes annual numbers-at-age, catch-at-age, biomass-at-age, F-at-age and natural-mortality outputs. The report provides spawning output, recruitment and management quantities with uncertainty.
decision_reason: NOAA Stock SMART ID 14516 is the U.S. West Coast Rougheye/Blackspotted management complex, consisting of Sebastes aleutianus and Sebastes melanostictus treated as one assessment unit. No matching canonical stock record was found. The adopted 2025 assessment has a matching native Stock Synthesis bundle with catch totals, CAAL and survey age data, biological assumptions, and fitted age-specific outputs. Mark eligible for source curation and an explicitly approximate age-structured translation; it is one complex and must not be counted as two cases.
notes: The report covers U.S. waters from the U.S.-Canada border to the U.S.-Mexico border and treats the two species as one management complex because they are difficult to distinguish in catches. The model uses data through 2024, two sexes, 140 population ages, and one area. The report and native bundle identify Stock Synthesis 3.30.23.2. Cached sources and checksums are listed in source_cache/discovery_noaa_rougheye_2025/sources.csv.

stock_name: Rex sole - Eastern Gulf of Alaska
catch_age_evidence: The final 2026 assessment reports fishery catch biomass in tonnes from 1982 through August 2026 (Table 7 says August 29; page 9 says August 22 for the terminal catch cutoff), and sex-specific fishery age compositions in 1992, 1995, 1999, 2003, 2005, 2007, 2009, 2010, 2012 and 2014-2024. The compositions are sampled proportions, not catch numbers-at-age; reconstruction requires catch biomass and weight-at-age.
survey_age_evidence: The RACE bottom-trawl survey provides separate eastern and western-central biomass indices for 1984-1999 (triennial) and 2001-2025 (biennial), with conditional age-at-length data in 1984, 1987, 1993, 1999 and biennially from 2001-2025. Marginal age compositions are not in the objective function; an age-specific survey index would be a documented reconstruction, not the native likelihood. Table 7 ends in 2025 while page 11 labels 112,824 t as a 2026 survey estimate; verify the year.
weights_evidence: Sex- and area-specific growth is estimated. Fixed weight-length relationships are female alpha 1.35e-6, beta 3.44963 and male alpha 2.18e-6, beta 3.30571; weight at age depends on the growth curves. Confirm the exact final-run weight scale before import.
maturity_evidence: Female maturity uses a logistic size-at-maturity relationship: 50% at 351.7 mm, with slope 0.0392 per mm, converted to age using survey-based mean length-at-age.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is fixed at 0.17 per year for females and males; M is not estimated.
timing_evidence: The assessment is annual. The available proposed-run file has one 12-month season and assigns survey biomass observations to month 7, but it ends in 2024 and is not the final 2026 run. The SSC notes survey timing was misspecified in the SS3-to-SPoRC bridge; verify the final-run timing before translation and do not infer a year fraction yet.
output_evidence: Appendix F reports Model 25.1 numbers-at-age for 1982-2026 by two areas and sex, ages 0-20. It gives no uncertainty intervals and does not state the number scale in the heading. The report also gives spawning-biomass and recruitment results; a numeric F-at-age surface was not located. M is fixed at 0.17, not an estimated output.
decision_reason: The official 2026 full assessment is a two-area assessment for the current Gulf of Alaska unit. The Plan Team recommended Model 25.1 for harvest specifications and the SSC supported the recommendation. The assessment documents age compositions, conditional survey age-at-length, biological inputs, survey indices and comparable population outputs. The source quantities support curation, with transformations and run-matched input details to verify before import.
notes: NOAA IDs 10058, 15410 and 15411 are grouped as one unit: 10058 is the legacy Gulf-wide entry; 15410 and 15411 are eastern and western-central area entries. NOAA ID 10059 Pacific Coast rex sole is a separate unit. The public AFSC repository at revision 453e1166e1bf83b9062fe228b93f2225b1cbe1aa contains proposed runs ending in 2024, not run-matched final 2026 files. The final-report-linked Appendix E attachment is marked draft; confirm its correspondence to the final model before importing values. See the source review and ignored source_cache/discovery_noaa_goa_rex_2026/sources.csv.

catch_age_evidence: The 2026 ISC assessment fits fleet catch by year and quarter, reported in metric tonnes or thousands of fish, plus size compositions. It does not fit observed catch-at-age; catch-at-age in model outputs is derived and cannot replace a source age composition.
survey_age_evidence: The base case fits one aggregate standardized CPUE index, Japanese longline Area 2 Quarter 2 (F10, 1996-2024); it is a fishery index, not a survey. No age-specific index or age-composition likelihood is reported.
weights_evidence: The model uses non-sex-specific seasonal weight-at-length relationships (kg from fork length in cm). It does not report a fitted weight-at-age input; conversion would require the model sex-specific growth distribution.
maturity_evidence: Female maturity is assumed to be 50% at age 5 and 100% at ages 6+, based on length at 50% maturity of 86 cm fork length.
mortality_evidence: Base-case natural mortality is fixed by age and sex: a Lorenzen size-based schedule for ages 0-2, common to both sexes until age 3, then 0.38 per year for males and 0.49 per year for females.
timing_evidence: The population model is quarterly; spawning and recruitment occur in Quarter 2 (April-June). The fitted F10 index also represents Quarter 2. There is no survey timing because the base-case index is fishery-derived.
output_evidence: The 2026 report provides annual numeric estimates for age-1+ biomass, female SSB and recruitment through 2024, with uncertainty. candidate_id: DFO:National Capital Region:Bluefin Tuna - Western Atlantic
catch_age_evidence: The 2021 Stock Synthesis advice model uses fleet catches in metric tonnes for 1950-2020 and size compositions. Conditional age-at-length data from otolith age-length pairs cover 1973-2018; 6,552 pairs remain after the strict-update screening. Japan longline catch-at-age was supplied only for diagnostics, not fitted in the likelihood. The report does not publish run-matched numeric catch-at-age or composition arrays.
survey_age_evidence: The model uses 12 aggregate relative-abundance indices, including the Gulf of St. Lawrence acoustic index, with within-year timing adjustments. The report documents fishery and survey age-length samples but no age-specific survey-index likelihood. Exact index timing and numeric age-composition inputs require the run-matched electronic files.
weights_evidence: Growth is estimated with a Richards model; the model uses the overall length-weight relationship 1.52e-5 * length^3.05305 to derive weight. A run-matched numeric weight-at-age surface was not found in the public assessment tables.
maturity_evidence: The model uses alternative early- and late-spawning maturity-at-age vectors for its two advice scenarios. SSB is the mass of mature fish; the vectors are tabulated for ages 0-35+.
mortality_evidence: Natural mortality is age-specific and follows a Lorenzen function scaled to M=0.1 per year at age 20; the report tabulates the resulting ages 0-35+ schedule.
timing_evidence: The model uses an annual time step and continuous removals. Each of the 12 abundance indices is adjusted for within-year timing, but the exact fractions are not enumerated in the report and remain to be checked in the run-matched model files.
output_evidence: The advice model reports SSB, recruitment, biomass and fishing-mortality trajectories through 2020 in figures, plus terminal F-based status and uncertainty in tables. It shows estimated F-at-age in a figure, but numeric annual N-at-age and F-at-age arrays were not located. Numeric VPA age-specific tables are not advice outputs.
decision_reason: The NOAA and DFO inventory entries describe the same Western Atlantic bluefin stock assessed by ICCAT; no canonical stock record was found. ICCAT identifies the 2021 Stock Synthesis model (1950-2020) as the model used for advice, and the 2024 SCRS summary still reports status from that assessment. The VPA supplied age-specific tables but was rejected for quantitative status and projection advice. The advice model includes conditional age-at-length information, but exact numerical input arrays, age-specific survey observations, and numeric age-specific outputs were not recovered from the public documents. Eligibility remains unresolved pending run-matched electronic inputs or a source-supported reconstruction.
notes: NOAA Stock SMART ID 10165 and the DFO Western Atlantic bluefin survey entry are linked as one transboundary ICCAT unit. The ICCAT assessment calendar lists the West Atlantic assessment as 2021/2027 and Stock Synthesis 3.30.14. Public reports and their checksummed source manifest are cached locally under source_cache/discovery_iccat_western_bluefin_2021/. No canonical database values were changed.

survey_age_evidence: The spring acoustic survey produces aggregate biomass and abundance indices. weights_evidence: The 2025 detailed report plots spring acoustic mean weights at ages 1-6 for 1985-2024 and describes fishery length-to-weight conversions. Numeric annual weight-at-age arrays were not found.
maturity_evidence: The source reports the proportion of female age-2 fish maturing in the spring acoustic survey, including a 2025 value of 34%. This is not a full age-by-sex maturity matrix.
mortality_evidence: No age-specific natural-mortality assumption or fitted M surface is reported. The maximum-F index combines the mature fraction of the acoustic biomass index with landings; it is not a population-model estimate of F-at-age.
timing_evidence: The spring acoustic survey is typically conducted in May (May 6-24 in 2024); the inshore commercial fishery runs June-August. The index forecast is not an age-structured population model with observation timing parameters.

decision_reason: This is a distinct current DFO stock complex with extensive age-specific survey and biological information. survey_age_evidence: The 2023 SSM report provides survey mean numbers per tow at ages 0-10+ with survey-specific year coverage: Canadian Autumn 2J3K, Canadian Spring and Autumn 3LNO, EU 3M surveys, and EU-Spain 3NO. weights_evidence: Catch weights-at-age (kg) for ages 1-10+ are tabulated in the 2023 SSM report. The companion SCAA report also provides catch weights-at-age and states that pre-1975 values use the 1975-1979 average. These are source-reported age-specific biological inputs.
maturity_evidence: The 2023 SCAA report provides a proportion-mature-at-age table used by its age-structured model. The SSM base-case specification is separate and does not imply a maturity-at-age likelihood.

timing_evidence: The 2023 SSM survey observation equation uses each survey-year midpoint as a fraction of year. Exact survey-year midpoint values were not recovered from the reviewed report and need verification from source survey dates or native files before an exact translation.

timing_evidence: The 2022 model places trap CPUE at fraction 0.5 of the year and the surveys at fraction 0.75, consistent with their October-November timing.

catch_age_evidence: The 2021 Stock Synthesis assessment uses annual commercial catch estimates from 1935-2021 and commercial age-frequency samples from 28 years (1979-2019). Bottom and midwater trawl data are combined as one fishery. Quarterly age compositions were catch-weighted and expanded using quarterly landings; catch-at-age therefore requires a documented reconstruction. Numeric input matrices were not found as separate public files in this screen.
survey_age_evidence: The model uses four aggregate trawl biomass-index series (QCS, WCVI, WCHG, and GIG) covering 1967-2020 and survey age compositions from 25 years across the four surveys. Survey age data are downweighted to 0.25; aggregate indices and age compositions could support a documented age-index reconstruction.
weights_evidence: Sex-specific growth and length-weight relationships were estimated from survey biological samples and fixed over time. The report gives growth and allometric parameters needed to derive weight-at-age for model ages 1-60.
maturity_evidence: The model uses a time-invariant female maturity ogive: zero at ages 1-4, a fitted monotonic curve at ages 5-16, and 1.0 from age 17 through the age-60 accumulator. The source describes the biological samples and fitted form.
mortality_evidence: The composite base case pools five component runs with fixed scalar M values of 0.04, 0.045, 0.05, 0.055, and 0.06. An estimated-M sensitivity had poor MCMC diagnostics and is not the adopted central run. M is not age-specific.
timing_evidence: The assessment is annual. It defines spawning biomass at the start of the year and exploitation rate in mid-year. Exact fractional timing for each survey observation was not verified in the published report.
output_evidence: The official composite base case reports annual female spawning-biomass and age-0 recruitment trajectories with posterior intervals through 2022, plus tabulated terminal B2022 quantiles. Numeric N-at-age and instantaneous F-at-age arrays were not recovered; reported fishing pressure is exploitation.
decision_reason: DFO identifies the 2021 assessment as the latest detailed coastwide age-structured assessment found for this unit. The 2025/26 IFMP anticipated an update in 2024, but no later detailed Yellowmouth assessment was found in the current DFO Pacific plan or CSAS search. The 2021 report documents catch totals and age compositions, four survey indices and survey age data, biology, mortality scenarios, and official SSB/recruitment outputs. These support source curation with documented reconstruction; original numeric age matrices and exact survey timing remain source-recovery tasks.
notes: The assessment is coastwide across PMFC areas 3CD and 5ABCDE and excludes 4B. It is a two-sex Stock Synthesis 3 assessment, ages 1-60, with one combined commercial trawl fishery and five fixed-M composite component runs. Age compositions are plotted in the report; no native run bundle was found in the public source search. Preserve the composite-base-case identity and distinguish its reported exploitation from instantaneous F-at-age.
